test_policy.notes: International students are exempt: the international page says ACT or SAT is not required for international admission. Domestic freshmen under 21 need a 2.25 high school GPA or ACT 21 (the Common Data Set gives ACT 21 or SAT 1060 as the alternative).

requirements.notes: Pitt State's own application; $60 non-refundable fee for undergraduate, graduate, exchange and IEP applicants. International high school applicants need a diploma and a minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent). Financial documents: a certified bank statement or financial guarantee dated within 6 months plus the Financial Statement of Support form; deposit amounts are in linked PDFs. Nursing majors born outside the US must submit a TOEFL iBT (cannot be waived).

deadlines.label: International fall 2027 application deadline
deadlines.notes: International deadlines are June 1 (fall, August start) and October 15 (spring, January start). The page gives no year, so June 1 is assumed to be 2027 for fall 2027 entry. No summer deadline is listed for degree programs. Domestic freshman dates (Feb. 1 application/ACT checklist date, Nov. 1 scholarship priority) are on the requirements page.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Paper and institutional (ITP) TOEFL scores are not accepted. The page lists no country or credential exemptions. Students without a passing score can often be admitted conditionally to most programs and must finish the highest level of the Intensive English Program (IEP) before academic coursework; the IEP Academic Preparation Course is equivalent to TOEFL 79 and can replace the test for more programs. IEP intakes: fall, spring and summer (8-week option at intermediate level with special permission). Duolingo ($49) can be used for IEP pre-assessment.

english.notes: Institution code 6336. Communication, Psychology and ESOL need 79 (15 per section); Nursing needs 79 with Writing 20, Speaking 20, Reading 19, Listening 20. The page does not give a new 1-6 scale minimum.
Communication, Psychology and ESOL need 6.5 (5.5 per section).

The page prints '100 per section'; Communication, Psychology and ESOL need 110. No school code needed (pick Pittsburg State University in the Duolingo database). A 2025-26 international brochure was not readable as text, so the table on the web page is used.

aid.notes: Gorilla International Scholarship for new international freshmen and transfers in degree programs: up to $6,000 per year by GPA (3.8-4.0 $6,000; 3.6-3.79 $5,000; 3.4-3.59 $4,000; 3.2-3.39 $3,000; 2.7-3.19 $2,000), a tuition waiver for up to four years of full-time enrollment, rescindable if cumulative GPA falls below 3.0, not valid in summer. English test scores, activities and need are also factors; no deadline is printed. An International Academic Excellence Scholarship also exists (no amount listed). The Common Data Set marks both need-based and non-need-based institutional aid as available to nonresidents.

cost.notes: Costs page, 2026-27, per year (2 x semester amounts): nonresident flat-rate tuition including campus fees $10,114 per semester = $20,228 (resident $4,442 per semester = $8,884); residence hall living estimate $5,317 per semester = $10,634 (no meal plan is listed); books and supplies $500 per semester = $1,000. International table adds sickness/accident insurance $2,661 and orientation/SEVIS compliance $80 (extra fees $2,741), for an estimated international academic-year total of $34,603. International students are charged the nonresident rate
